To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the use of a domain-ontology in an e-learning environment is a promising approach and that semantic search is a very promising technique for retrieving learning material.
semantic search is more efficient than full text search and that it works for all languages.

(1) semantic search outperforms full-text search for all languages; (2) the domain ontology can be constructed and maintained by a small group of experts, but requires the collaboration of several language experts to create the lexicons; (3) the domain ontology is not only useful for semantic search, but also for other applications such as the management of learning objects.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the integration of semantic knowledge into an existing e-Learning system to improve the search for learning objects in the system.
the integration of language technologies into eLearning environments.
the development of a domain-ontology and its application in an eLearning context.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
semantic search has a clear advantage for the German language.
semantic search can be a useful and effective tool for the retrieval of learning objects, but only if it is based on a domain ontology that is carefully designed and implemented.
the use of semantic knowledge in an e-learning environment can be beneficial for the learner and the teacher.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
semantic knowledge is a valuable asset for eLearning, especially in a multilingual environment.
semantic search is an effective method for retrieving learning material in different languages.
the integration of semantic search into a learning management system can be a valuable tool in an e-learning environment.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the integration of semantic knowledge in a learning management system can be done in a way that it can be used by all languages and all users.
semantic search can improve cross-lingual information retrieval and that the domain-ontology is a good basis for the annotation of learning material in different languages.
the semantic annotation of learning objects with a domain-ontology can be done in a language-independent way.
